newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Filipino "healing nun" wins Magsaysay prize.
newsitem.headline: Filipino "healing nun" wins Magsaysay prize.

text.p: A Filipina Roman Catholic nun who runs free health clinics in Manila's squatter colonies and gives shelter to street children and rape-victims was named winner on Monday of the Ramon Magsaysay Award for community leadership.
Sister Eva Fidela Maamo, 56, a surgeon, was cited for "her compelling example in bringing humane assistance and the healing arts to the poorest Filipinos," the Magsaysay foundation said.

Maamo began working for the poor in mid-1970s when she set up a crude bamboo clinic on southern Mindanao island, performing operations on tribesmen by flashlight and using coconut water for dextrose, in the absence of medical supplies, it said.

Maamo is the third winner of the Magsaysay prize for this year. The others are Thailand's former prime minister Anand Panyarachun, for government service, and Indian environmentalist lawyer Mahesh Chander Mehta, winner of the public service prize.
The award was established in 1958 in honour of a popular Philippine president who died in an aircrash in 1957. The award carries a cash prize of $50,000.
The foundation has yet to announce the winners for journalism-literature and for international understanding.
